claim: The card's own subject, stated by the framework: an extensible specification systems use to interoperate over lineage metadata.
query: OpenLineage open framework data lineage collection analysis extensible specification
snippet: OpenLineage is an open framework for data lineage collection and analysis. At its core is an extensible specification that systems can use to interoperate with lineage metadata.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: What lineage is, as the framework states it

claim: Lineage here is recorded about a job in execution, which is what ties this card to a run rather than to a stored artifact.
query: OpenLineage open standard lineage metadata collection record job in execution
snippet: OpenLineage is an Open Standard for lineage metadata collection designed to record metadata for a job in execution.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: What the standard records

claim: Three entities - dataset, job, run - plus facets as the extension point. This is the card's noun set.
query: OpenLineage generic model dataset job run entities naming strategies facets
snippet: The standard defines a generic model of dataset, job, and run entities uniquely identified using consistent naming strategies. The core model is highly extensible via facets.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: The entity model the card's inputs and outputs live in

claim: The operation set is an event stream with a stated minimum: START plus one terminal event. Everything else is optional.
query: OpenLineage Run Event START COMPLETE FAIL ABORT required additional optional
snippet: **Run Event**: an event describing an observed state of a job run. Sending at least a START event and a COMPLETE/FAIL/ABORT event is required. Additional events are optional.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The minimum event set a producer must emit

claim: Six run states, each with the condition it signals - the value domain a lineage consumer branches on.
query: OpenLineage six run states START RUNNING COMPLETE ABORT FAIL OTHER
snippet: There are six run states currently defined in the OpenLineage spec: START to indicate the beginning of a Job RUNNING to provide additional information about a running Job COMPLETE to signify that execution of the Job has concluded ABORT to signify that the Job has been stopped abnormally FAIL to signify that the Job has failed OTHER to send additional metadata outside standard run cycle
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The run state domain

claim: The order half of the operation set: three states are terminal and a terminal event closes the run.
query: OpenLineage accumulative events COMPLETE ABORT FAIL terminal no other events
snippet: Unless specified otherwise, we assume events describing a single run are accumulative and COMPLETE, ABORT and FAIL are terminal events. Sending any of terminal events means no other events related to this run will be emitted.
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: Which states are terminal and what follows one

claim: OTHER is explicitly exempt from the ordering, which is why the order cannot be asserted as a simple sequence.
query: OpenLineage OTHER sent anytime before terminal states before START
snippet: Additionally, we allow OTHER to be sent anytime before the terminal states, also before START.
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The one state with no position in the order

claim: A facet is the card's configurable unit: metadata attached to one of the three entities.
query: OpenLineage facet piece of metadata attached to core entities
snippet: **Facet**: A piece of metadata attached to one of the entities defined above.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The extension point's unit

claim: Facets are last-write-wins per name per entity, not merged - a behaviour a consumer must know to read a run correctly.
query: OpenLineage facet atomic identified by name replaces previous facet instance entirely
snippet: A facet is an atomic piece of metadata identified by its name. This means that emitting a new facet with the same name for the same entity replaces the previous facet instance for that entity entirely.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: Facet write semantics

claim: A caller extending the vocabulary must prefix by project, which is the collision rule that makes extension safe.
query: OpenLineage custom facets distinct prefix project defining avoid collision standard facets
snippet: Custom facets must use a distinct prefix named after the project defining them to avoid collision with standard facets
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The namespacing rule for caller-defined metadata

claim: The legal shape of a caller-defined word at this card, given as a pattern rather than a list.
query: OpenLineage naming custom facets pattern prefix name entity Facet PascalCase
snippet: Naming of custom facets should follow the pattern `{prefix}{name}{entity}Facet` PascalCased.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The naming pattern a custom facet must follow

claim: The vocabulary is open-ended by design and has a stated promotion path, which is unusual among the standards profiled here.
query: OpenLineage custom facets promoted to the standard included in spec
snippet: Custom facets can be promoted to the standard by including them in the spec.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: How a caller's word becomes part of the standard

claim: The scope statement names the transport as configurable, which makes protocol the declared - and therefore cosmetic - variation point rather than the real swap axis.
query: OpenLineage scope defines metadata running jobs configurable backend choose protocol
snippet: OpenLineage defines the metadata for running jobs and their corresponding events. A configurable backend allows the user to choose what protocol to send the events to.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: The standard's own scope, and what it leaves configurable

claim: One field decides which lifecycle a consumer should expect, which is where the genuine swap axis is declared.
query: OpenLineage JobTypeJobFacet processingType field lifecycle characteristics
snippet: Jobs can have different processing types that define their lifecycle characteristics. The JobTypeJobFacet processingType field indicates the nature of the job:
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The field that declares a job's lifecycle kind

claim: A batch job is expected to end, so a consumer may wait for a terminal event.
query: OpenLineage BATCH jobs finite clear start end expected terminate naturally
snippet: BATCH jobs are finite jobs with a clear start and end point. They are expected to terminate naturally after completing their work.
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The finite lifecycle

claim: A streaming job has no completion point, so the same consumer waiting for a terminal event would wait forever.
query: OpenLineage STREAMING jobs continuous process data streams indefinitely no natural completion
snippet: STREAMING jobs are continuous jobs that process data streams indefinitely with no natural completion point.
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The continuous lifecycle

claim: The standard tells a consumer outright that the terminal events are unreliable here - a difference in what can be read back, not a label.
query: OpenLineage streaming START COMPLETE ABORT FAIL should not be relied upon restarted
snippet: While START, COMPLETE, ABORT, or FAIL events can be emitted, they should not be relied upon as they might occur only occasionally when the streaming job is restarted
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: What a consumer may not rely on under the continuous lifecycle

claim: The second axis of the same swap: whether one event can be read alone or only in combination with the rest of the run.
query: OpenLineage eventCompleteness field emission pattern what information events contain
snippet: The eventCompleteness field in the emission pattern describes what information events contain:
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The field that declares how much one event contains

claim: Under snapshot completeness a single event stands alone, which is the opposite reading discipline from accumulative events.
query: OpenLineage complete snapshot events self-contained for its time period
snippet: Each event is self-contained for its time period
title: The Run Cycle | OpenLineage
topic: The self-contained event

claim: The named reference implementation of the API this card's evidence rests on.
query: Marquez LF AI DATA project collect aggregate visualize metadata reference implementation OpenLineage API
snippet: Marquez: Marquez is an LF AI & DATA project to collect, aggregate, and visualize a data ecosystem's metadata. It is the reference implementation of the OpenLineage API.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: The reference implementation

claim: The pre-standard state: every producer writing its own collector, which is the cost the card's standard removes.
query: OpenLineage each project instrument custom metadata collection integration duplicating efforts
snippet: Each project has to instrument its own custom metadata collection integration, therefore duplicating efforts.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: The problem the standard exists to remove

claim: The stated benefit, and the reason the producer side rather than the backend is where this card's value sits.
query: OpenLineage integration efforts shared across projects
snippet: Integration efforts are shared across projects.
title: About OpenLineage | OpenLineage
topic: What the standard buys

claim: A run is identified by a globally unique id scoped to its job definition, which is the join a lineage query needs.
query: OpenLineage Run instance running job globally unique ID relative to job definition
snippet: **Run**: An instance of a running job with a start and completion (or failure) time. A run is identified by a globally unique ID relative to its job definition.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The run identity rule

claim: The card's only typed failure detail: a run facet carrying the message, language and optional stack trace when a run fails.
query: OpenLineage errorMessage facet error message programming language stack trace run fails
snippet: **errorMessage**: Captures the error message, programming language - and optionally stack trace - when a run fails.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: The typed failure carrier

claim: The facet that makes a lineage graph out of nested runs, and the nearest thing at this card to a run-id correlation rule.
query: OpenLineage parent facet parent job and run spawned from parent run
snippet: **parent**: Captures the parent job and run when the run has been spawned from a parent run.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: How a child run names its parent

claim: The provenance half of the card: a run can name the code version that produced it, by git sha.
query: OpenLineage sourceCodeLocation facet source code location version git sha job
snippet: **sourceCodeLocation**: Captures the source code location and version (e.g., git sha) of the job.
title: OpenLineage Spec (spec/OpenLineage.md, raw)
topic: How a run points at the code that produced it
